key_insight: Agentic Imagination (Agima) trains a single model to propose actions, visualize their consequences, and reason over imagined futures before acting.
engineering_relevance: Imagined rollouts could support planning when real-world feedback is sparse or actions are difficult to reverse.
method: Use supervised fine-tuning to unify action selection and image-based world modeling in one omni model.
Simulate action sequences and branch into alternatives to compare possible futures.
Apply agentic reinforcement learning to learn when and where imagination helps planning.
evidence_signal: Across Maze2D, Sokoban, Pacman, and PushT, Agima generalizes to harder unseen settings; SFT-only training on two-box Sokoban yields 40% success on four-box puzzles versus 2% for an action-only planner, with real-board observations every five moves.
watch_item: Evaluation covers four environments; transfer to real-world tasks and robustness to errors in imagined outcomes remain unestablished.
